A July 2026 paper in Atmospheric Chemistry and Physics by Marjani, Mehrdad and Quaas simulated aircraft contrails inside natural cirrus. Persistent contrails embedded in existing cirrus can survive, change the host cloud's humidity and ice, and in very moist, unstable air even spread upward above flight level.

Under a high deck, do not leave at the moment of sunset. Keep watching for 10 to 20 minutes, and turn around now and then: if the Sun finds a gap below the cloud edge, the underside of the deck overhead can light up pink after the horizon has gone dull.

On October 9, 1992, at about 7:50 PM EDT, just after sunset, a fireball crossed West Virginia and Pennsylvania heading north-northeast and dropped a 12.4 kg stone through the trunk of a parked car in Peekskill, New York. Sixteen separate videos, many shot by fans at a high school football game, captured it.

In June 2026 the German space agency DLR described how its TerraSAR-X and TanDEM-X radar satellites, flying as close as about 200 m apart at 505 km, ride out storms. Storms can raise air density at that height about tenfold, from 1 to 10 g per cubic km. After 2024 storms upset the pair, DLR switched to a mix of three forecast models, and both kept working through the January and February 2026 storms.

The same sunspot group behind this CME, Region 4549, also fired a flare that caused an R2 radio blackout at 11:48 AM EDT on October 8. A flare's X-rays reach Earth in about 8 minutes, while the cloud of solar material it may launch takes days.

facts.text: The predicted peak, about 9 PM EDT, lands right at the best viewing time for this shower. Unlike most showers, the Draconids favour the evening because Draco stands high in the north after dusk. Give it 20 to 30 minutes in a lawn chair; meteors from this comet are slow and often faint.

In March 2026 the Global Meteor Network reported a new shower in Dorado, with a speed of 17.3 km/s and a Jupiter-family comet orbit. The Draconid parent, 21P/Giacobini-Zinner, is also a Jupiter-family comet, and its debris is similarly slow, which is why Draconids drift rather than streak.

Comet 21P was found by Michel Giacobini in Nice in December 1900, then lost. Ernst Zinner recovered it on October 23, 1913, which is why it carries both names, and why the shower is sometimes called the Giacobinids.

Draconid meteoroids reach Earth at only about 20 km/s because they catch up to us from behind, rather than meeting us head on like the 66 km/s Orionids. The parent comet's nucleus is only about 2 km across, yet it sheds enough dust to have produced two great storms, in 1933 and 1946.

A 2026 paper by Daniel Toledo, posted in May and published in Atmospheric Measurement Techniques in September, explains why twilight colour changes in a measurable way when high cloud is present. The sky's colour peaks at a Sun angle that depends on how high the cloud is, so twilight hues can be used to estimate cloud height.

After sunset the ground is in shadow while high clouds are still in direct sunlight. Because sunlight reaches them at a shallow angle through a long air path that strips out blue, they glow red or orange, and the higher the cloud, the longer it keeps its colour.

Open-Meteo's layer data shows 0% low, mid and high cloud at sunset. With no cloud at any height there is nothing to catch the light, so the colour stays in the sky's own gradient. Sunrise tomorrow is 7:16 AM and sunset 6:40 PM, so the days are shortening by about two minutes a day.

facts.text: NOAA's two products disagree on timing. The 3-day text puts Kp 5.0 at 11 PM to 2 AM and 5.67 from 5 AM to 8 AM, while the JSON forecast puts the 5.67 peak around 2 AM. Both agree on the maximum, which stays under the Kp 7 line for this latitude.

A CME's effect depends on its magnetic field. If the field points south when it reaches Earth, it connects with Earth's field and pours energy in; if it points north, much of the storm fizzles. That is only measurable about an hour before arrival, so forecast Kp can change on the night.

A July 2026 simulation study of radiation fog in Italy's Po Valley found that more aerosol particles mean more, smaller droplets that settle more slowly, keeping fog around up to 54 minutes longer.

In July 2026, smoke from Canadian wildfires turned New England skies yellow. Smoke particles absorb blue and violet light and let yellow, orange and red through, and the thicker the smoke, the stronger the tint.
Smoke and dust particles are much larger than air molecules and scatter light by Mie scattering. The effect is strongest at sunrise and sunset, when sunlight crosses the most air.

facts.text: The shower runs October 6-10, so a few Draconids can appear tonight. Watch from nightfall to midnight, when the radiant near Eltanin and Rastaban is highest in the northern sky.
In July 2026 the Global Meteor Network found a new shower in Scorpius, M2026-P1. It identified 43 of its meteors using 114 cameras in five countries and traced them to a Jupiter-family comet orbit.
The Draconids produced storms of several thousand meteors an hour in 1933 and 1946. In 2011 watchers in Europe saw more than 600 an hour.

On October 7, 1959, Luna 3 took the first photographs of the Moon's far side. It shot 29 pictures on film, developed them on board and scanned them back to Earth, covering about 70% of the hidden hemisphere.

facts.text: NOAA's forecast issued October 7 expects quiet conditions tonight, then minor to moderate storms on October 9 when a CME launched on October 6 arrives.

The January 19, 2026 storm reached G4 after one of the fastest CMEs in decades, but its magnetic field (Bz) turned strongly northward. That limited the energy reaching Earth, and auroras stayed mostly at high latitudes.

Even on the October 9 storm night, NOAA's top forecast of Kp 5.67 is below the level usually needed here. A camera on a long exposure, aimed north from a dark spot, will pick up faint red glow that the eye misses.

facts.text: The air is very dry and clear but turbulent, with seeing at 6 on a scale where 8 is worst. Expect strong twinkling near the horizon. It is a good night for wide views and the Milky Way, and a soft one for telescope detail on Saturn until the air steadies a little toward dawn.
EarthSky notes that shortly before sunrise on October 7 and 8 the thin waning Moon glows in the east below Jupiter and Regulus, a day after the Moon passed in front of Jupiter.

quiz.explain: Seeing is about turbulence in the air: poor seeing makes stars twinkle and smears fine detail in a telescope, while transparency is the separate measure of how clear the air is.
options: How steady the air is, which sets how much stars twinkle and blur
How dark the sky is away from city lights
How much moisture and haze is dimming faint stars
